title: OpenAI compat: tool metadata enrichment and deterministic choice tiebreaker
author: Anjali Patel
description: Summary: This PR augments the OpenAI compatibility layer for function/tool calling with two focused changes: (1) a small, backwards-compatible enrichment of tool metadata emitted in the 'tool_choice' decision path so integrators can better map platform tools to OpenAI-style schemas, and (2) a deterministic tiebreaker for tool_choice when multiple candidate tools score equally. Motivation: downstream consumers and analytics consistently asked for richer tool descriptors in the compatibility envelope (origin, semantic tags, and a lightweight version field) to make tool routing and telemetry more reliable. Separately, nondeterministic selection when scores tie led to flaky integration tests and occasional user-visible variability in multi-tool flows; we add a deterministic tie-break strategy that preserves operator-configurable preferences and causal ordering. Design highlights: - Tool metadata enrichment: the compatibility adapter now includes an optional metadata block on each candidate tool in the selection envelope: {"origin","tags","schema_version"} (enrichment is only added for OpenAI-compatible envelopes and gated behind a feature flag). This is strictly additive and will not change existing schema parsing flows. - Deterministic tiebreaker: when two or more tools have equivalent selection scores, we apply the following deterministic comparator (in priority order): 1) explicit_developer_priority (if present, higher wins), 2) tool_registration_time (older wins to favor stable integrations), 3) lexicographic on tool_id as final tie-break (stable but arbitrary). This comparator is deterministic across runs and safe for replay. - Streaming message framing: when emitting the 'tool_choice' event over streaming, we now append the minimal metadata fingerprint rather than the entire metadata blob to reduce token pressure; the full metadata is available via the non-streamed final envelope. - Backwards compatibility and opt-in: feature-flagged behind `compat.tool_metadata_enrichment` and `compat.tool_choice_tiebreak`. When not enabled, behavior is identical to prior releases. - Telemetry and monitoring: new metrics added: openai.compat.tool_choice.tiebreaks, openai.compat.tool_choice.metadata_emitted, and a histogram of tiebreak reasons. We also log a low-volume sampling of pre/post selection snapshots for regression triage. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for comparator ordering, including edge cases (missing developer priorities, identical registration timestamps). - Integration tests for streaming envelopes that ensure a) streaming fragment size remains within SLO, and b) clients that ignore the new metadata still process tool_call events correctly. - End-to-end QA: validated against r/w external example app that uses two equivalent scoring tools; repeated runs are deterministic after the change. Migration and rollout: - Default state: feature flags off for 1 week while we stage canary traffic. - Canary on 10% traffic (redwood-hosted) for 48 hours, monitor tiebreak histogram and false-positive tool_invocations. - If stable, flip enrichment flag for all hosted customers; Private/Dedicated customers can toggle at will. Risk assessment: - Small risk: some clients may have relied on prior nondeterministic behavior (unlikely). - Low risk: added metadata increases envelope size; mitigated by streaming fingerprint approach. Related: closes ENG-4521 and ties into PM-228 prompt-engineering work. See docs/compat/openai-tool-calls.md for operator-facing notes.

f14b2c3: emit tool metadata enrichment in compat adapter behind feature flag
d3f45ee: streaming: emit metadata fingerprint on tool_choice fragments
b29a7a1: docs: compatibility notes and rollout guide
e4c1d2f: add telemetry counters and histogram for tiebreaks
release_notes: Add opt-in tool metadata enrichment for OpenAI compat envelopes and deterministically resolve tied tool_choice scores; telemetry and docs included.
review_comments: Marcus Nguyen (review): Could we ensure the tiebreak respects an explicit developer-configured ordering stored on the tool registration? If so, document that priority is authoritative. -- Reply (Anjali): yes, we added explicit_developer_priority as the top comparator and documented it in the adapter README.

Riley Thompson (review): Streaming fragments look good but I worry about clients that inspect the streamed payload for routing. We should emit a compact fingerprint and provide a lookup endpoint. -- Reply (Anjali): added fingerprint emission and updated SDK helper to fetch the full metadata lazily; added integration tests.
Leah Kim (approve): Tests are comprehensive and metric names look consistent with the telemetry conventions. Approved after small nits on docs.

QA (comment): Found flakiness when two tools had identical registration timestamps. The lexicographic fallback produces stable but unexpected ordering; added test to assert stability. -- Reply (Anjali): added test and expanded rollout notes to call out timestamp deduping guidance.
